profile.headline: Full Stack developer for Microsoft platforms.
profile.summary:
I am a full stack developer with 20+ years of experience working mainly with Microsoft platforms to develop business and public facing applications to support public health efforts. I have experience building out new platforms, migrating platforms and building out services that provide communication between platforms. 

A recent project required an extremely reliable, extremely performant solution to handle content publication for a government website with a large public presence. I was able to craft a queue- based multi-threaded service that monitors its own load and can ramp up resources as needed to provide timely processing of content updates. Comprehensive logging traces every step of the process so that debugging any issue is very easy to understand.

Another project put me in a spot where I had to shore up a website development effort that was not going well. I was able to drop into the project, build out a supporting API and learn React.js in time to rescue the development of the front-end and deliver the project on time.

My recent efforts have been spent migrating .Net applications to Microsoft Power Platform. This has been challenging as Power Platform is very good for a lot of simple things, but requires some creativity to solve the edge cases that come up in regular .Net development. I've been learning how to meet these needs over the last year and how to do it with some efficiency.

I've historically been placed on projects with a minimum of guidance and oversite where I would interface with the customer directly for instruction about what was needed. I've been good in these roles, with an eye on managing scope creep and able to find the undocumented requirements essential to a project's success. I can learn skills as needed, especially when given a working system or something that needs to be reverse engineered. I've also spent some years mentoring as needed to get junior developers up to speed on technology, process and SOP.
